question: Earliest bit/byte stored and sent through a transistor

findings.finding: Bardeen and Brattain transistor device successfully amplified electrical signals at Bell Labs. Not documented as the first digital bit stored or sent.
Audio amplification demonstrated to Bell Labs leadership; no digital byte involved.
Manchester transistor computer demonstrated running programs with transistorized logic; main storage was a magnetic drum.
Computer History Museum documents transistor registers and small memory circuitry in early computers. Exact first stored digital bit via a transistor not identified.

boundaries: A transistor can transmit or amplify an analog signal; no byte semantics follow.
A bistable transistor latch uses transistor circuitry to preserve one bit; a transistor by itself is not necessarily a memory cell.
Early Manchester machine's drum is not transistor-based main storage.
